summary: 创作《彼得兔》的比阿特丽克斯·波特自幼观察自然，也画过严谨的真菌插图。儿童书出版改变了她的生活，晚年她又把对田园的热爱转化为保护英国湖区土地的行动。

sentences: Beatrix Potter is one of the best-selling children’s authors of all time.
碧雅翠丝·波特是历来最畅销的儿童文学作家之一。
Her popular series of books that includes The Tale of Peter Rabbit was first published over one hundred years ago and has never been out of print.
她的系列作品包括《彼得兔的故事》，一百多年前首次出版后一直未曾绝版。
Generations of children have enjoyed her many stories and illustrations, all of which celebrate the English way of life and rural landscape through the adventures of animals.
几代儿童都喜爱她的故事和插图，它们借动物历险来赞美英格兰的生活方式和乡村风景。
paragraphs.gist: 波特用动物历险和亲绘插图呈现英格兰乡村生活，包括《彼得兔的故事》在内的作品一百多年来一直再版，陪伴了几代儿童。

paragraphs.brief: 独处童年与自创秘密日记
sentences: Born into a comfortable middle-class family in London in 1866, Potter spent much of her early life in her own company.
波特1866年生于伦敦一个家境舒适的中产家庭，早年大半时光独自度过。
She was educated at home by a governess and rarely saw her brother, Bertram, who was sent to boarding school.
她在家跟女家庭教师学习，弟弟伯特伦去了寄宿学校，两人很少见面。
Having little social contact with children of her own age, Potter was drawn into a private world of writing.
因少有同龄玩伴，波特沉浸在自己私人的写作世界。
When she was 15, she began to keep a diary written in a secret code of her own invention.
十五岁起，她用一套自创的密码记日记。
Even Beatrix herself, when she read back over it in later life, found it difficult to understand.
就连碧翠丝自己，晚年重读时也觉得很难看懂。
It was not until 15 years after her death that the code was cracked.
直到她去世十五年后，这套密码才被破解。
To the outside world Beatrix seemed shy and reserved, but in her diary she expressed herself freely and was critical of the work of several contemporary artists.
外人看来她腼腆含蓄，在日记里她却畅所欲言，还批评好几位当代艺术家的作品。
paragraphs.gist: 童年少有同龄玩伴的波特十五岁起用自创密码写日记，在众人眼中腼腆的她能在其中直言批评艺术家，密码直到她死后十五年才被破解。

paragraphs.brief: 动物绘画、真菌学与性别门槛
sentences: Potter was a naturally gifted artist, and with the aid of some art lessons she also learned the technical side of drawing.
波特天生有艺术才华，也通过一些美术课掌握了绘画技法。
Throughout her childhood she looked after many animals— rabbits, frogs and even bats—and sketched them constantly, gradually improving her work by sketching in museums.
童年时她照料兔子、青蛙乃至蝙蝠等许多动物，常为它们速写，又去博物馆临摹，不断精进画技。
She was also interested in natural history.
她还对博物学很感兴趣。
She would spend many hours drawing wildlife such as fungi and flowers, and at one time she had an ambition to develop this scientific interest.
她花许多时间描绘真菌、花草等野生生物，一度希望进一步钻研自然科学。
An uncle tried to help her enrol at the Royal Botanic Gardens at Kew in London, but she was rejected because of her gender.
一位叔叔曾想帮她进入伦敦的邱园皇家植物园学习，但她因是女性而被拒绝。
Nevertheless, she won respect from the scientific establishment for her illustrations and her contribution to mycology, the study of fungi.
尽管如此，她的插画和她对真菌学，也就是研究真菌的学科所作的贡献，仍赢得科学界尊重。
paragraphs.gist: 照料动物与长期写生磨炼了波特的绘画技巧，她虽因性别未能进入邱园深造，描绘真菌的图画和真菌学研究仍获学界尊重。

paragraphs.brief: 拒绝包办婚姻以保持独立
sentences: When Potter was in her early twenties, her parents tried to arrange a husband for her.
波特二十出头时，父母试图为她安排婚姻。
Many suitable suitors were found; however, Potter turned them all down.
他们物色了许多合适的对象，但波特一概谢绝。
Fiercely independent, she disliked the idea of being tied to a domestic life that, at that time, consisted mostly of staying at home and raising children.
她极为独立，不愿被当时以留在家中养育子女为主的家庭生活束缚。
Thus—unusually for British women of the period—she remained single and lived in her parents’ home.
因此她保持单身，住在父母家中，这在当时的英国女性中并不寻常。
paragraphs.gist: 二十出头时波特拒绝了父母安排的多位追求者，因为她珍惜独立，不愿把生活局限于持家育儿。

paragraphs.brief: 彼得兔出版与编辑协作
sentences: For several years Potter tried to get her first children’s book, The Tale of Peter Rabbit, published.
波特花了好几年，设法让自己的第一本童书《彼得兔的故事》得以出版。
Her initial attempts were unsuccessful, but she persevered, and eventually Frederick Warne & Co. accepted the book.
她的最初尝试没有成功，但她坚持，最后弗雷德里克·沃恩公司接受了这本书。
It was finally published in 1902, when Potter was 36, though the publishers did not expect it to sell many copies.
1902年，这本书终于在她三十六岁时出版，尽管出版商原本并不指望它畅销。
The project was given to the youngest brother in the firm, Norman Warne, as his first assignment—essentially a test.
这项工作交给了公司兄弟中最年轻的诺曼·沃恩，是他的第一项任务，实际上也算一次考验。
Luckily, he warmed to both the book and its author.
幸运的是，他对这本书及其作者都渐生好感。
Determined to make it a success, he worked closely with Potter, poring over every detail.
他决心使它获得成功，他与波特密切合作，仔细研究每一个细节。
It was Norman who insisted that each illustration should be in colour, while Potter insisted the book remain small enough for children to hold easily.
诺曼坚持每幅插图都要印成彩色，波特则坚持开本要小，好让孩子轻松拿在手里。
By the end of the year, 28,000 copies were in print.
到年底，印数已达两万八千册。
paragraphs.gist: 《彼得兔的故事》几经退稿才问世，编辑沃恩坚持彩色插图，波特坚持适合小手握持的开本，出版当年印数就达两万八千册。

sentences: The relationship between Warne and Potter blossomed, and they eventually became engaged.
沃恩与波特情愫渐深，最终订下婚约。
However, Potter’s parents disapproved because of his occupation.
但波特的父母不赞成，原因是沃恩的职业。
They relented only on condition that the couple live apart for six months to give Potter time to reconsider.
他们终于让步，条件是两人先分开六个月，让波特有机会重新考虑。
Tragically, before the wedding could take place, Warne developed pernicious anaemia, a blood disease, and passed away.
不幸的是，婚礼前沃恩患上恶性贫血这种血液疾病，因而去世。
Potter was devastated and wrote to his sister, Millie, “He did not live long, but he fulfilled a useful, happy life.
波特悲痛欲绝，给沃恩的妹妹米莉写信说：“他活得不长，却过了有意义、快乐的一生。
I must try to make a fresh beginning next year.”
我明年必须努力重新开始。”
paragraphs.gist: 沃恩和波特订婚后，她的父母因他的职业而要求两人分开半年，婚礼举行前他却因恶性贫血去世，使她深受打击。

paragraphs.brief: 湖区农场和遗赠的土地
sentences: After Warne’s death, Potter moved to the Lake District in northern England.
沃恩死后，波特搬到英格兰北部的湖区。
In 1905 she bought a small farm there, and for the next eight years she busied herself writing more books, some set in or around the area.
1905年她在那里买了一座小农场，接下来的八年忙于写更多书，有些故事就发生在农场及其周边。
She remained there for the rest of her life, but failing eyesight eventually forced her to stop writing children’s books.
她的余生都在那里，但视力不佳最终迫使她停止写儿童书籍。
Instead, she devoted herself to breeding sheep and helping to conserve farms in the district.
她转而专心养羊，也协助保护湖区的农场。
Thanks to the proceeds from her successful books and a later inheritance, Potter was able to buy many working farms.
凭着畅销书的收入和后来继承的遗产，波特购得多座仍在经营的农场。
On her death she left more than 4,000 acres to the National Trust, an organisation that protects historic buildings and countryside in England.
她去世时，把四千多英亩土地留给保护英格兰历史建筑和乡村的国民信托。
As a result, her beloved landscape is now accessible to countless visitors.
因此，如今有无数游客能亲身欣赏她所热爱的风景。
paragraphs.gist: 波特移居湖区后继续创作，视力衰退才转而养羊、保护农场，去世时把四千多英亩土地留给国民信托，让公众得以共享这片风景。

groups.instructionsZh: 先回想空格里的英文。每空填一个词。

items.en: The life of a typical married woman at that time appealed to Potter.
items.zh: 波特向往当时已婚女性通常过的生活。
items.why: 波特独立性很强，不愿被居家育儿的生活束缚，因此当时典型的婚后生活并不吸引她。

items.en: Potter’s publishers insisted on changing the title of her first book.
items.zh: 波特的出版商坚持要给她的第一本书换个书名。
items.why: 文中记下出版社对彩色插图的要求和波特对开本的坚持，没有提及要求改书名。

items.en: The publishers doubted whether Potter’s first book would be successful.
items.zh: 出版商怀疑波特的第一本书能否取得成功。
items.why: 出版商原先并不指望这本书能卖出很多本，正说明他们怀疑它的销路。

items.en: Norman Warne suggested Potter include black-and-white illustrations in her first book.
items.zh: 诺曼·沃恩建议波特在第一本书中加入黑白插图。
items.why: 诺曼坚持每幅插图都要采用彩色，题干却说他建议使用黑白插图。

items.en: At first, Potter’s parents disapproved of Norman Warne as a potential husband.
items.zh: 起初，波特的父母不赞成女儿与诺曼·沃恩结婚。
items.why: 波特的父母因诺曼的职业而最初反对这门婚事。

items.en: Potter continued writing children’s books until her death.
items.zh: 波特一直写儿童读物，直到去世为止。
items.why: 她虽在那里生活到去世，但视力衰退已迫使她提前停止写儿童读物。

items.en: Potter’s gift to the National Trust was the largest in recent times.
items.zh: 波特捐给国民信托的财产，是近些年该机构获赠的最大一笔。
items.why: 文中给出了她捐给国民信托的土地面积，没有与同期其他捐赠作比较，无法认定最大。

clauses: Generations of children have enjoyed her many stories and illustrations, ….
“all of which celebrate the English way of life and rural landscape through the adventures of animals”修饰前面的 stories。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 stories，再把修饰信息接回主句。
It was Norman who insisted …, while Potter insisted the book remain small enough for children to hold easily.
“that each illustration should be in colour”补足 insisted 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 insisted 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。
